lead: At the foot of Montjuïc, with historic theatres, Carrer de Blai and a lively, mixed, working-class atmosphere.
text: It began to be built around 1858 with simple little houses that owners put up for workers, and by about 1869 it was already laid out. That working-class origin lives on in a multicultural neighbourhood, with the Paral·lel theatres, such as El Molino, the Apolo, the Victòria and the Condal, Carrer de Blai with its pinchos bars, and the hill of Montjuïc a step away.

Living in El Poble-sec means having the hill, with its gardens and viewpoints, at your front door, and the Paral·lel, El Raval and Sant Antoni within walking distance. At an average sale price of 4,013 €/m² and a rent of 943 €/month, its figures are below those of Sants, even though the centre is just as close.
housing: Buildings from the late 19th and early 20th centuries, on streets sloping up towards Montjuïc.
